text:
caroline: FYI Ellen's engineering lead says their POC streaming is arriving as partial JSON chunks and the browser client chokes while parsing. Happens ~10-30s into a stream, intermittent. They see reconnects and sometimes half the event is missing. Can SEs help triage?

ellen: repro steps: we call Redwood hosted endpoint via our backend (node). On the client we use EventSource to parse SSE. When it fails we get `SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input` inside our onmessage handler. Sometimes we see `event: message\ndata: {\"delta\":\"...\"` then nothing. We pasted a capture below.

ellen: client console capture:
```
EventSource message: data: {\"delta\":\"The quick brown\"
// connection drops
// on reconnect we get remainder
EventSource message: data: \" fox jumps over...\"
```

sam: thanks. A few things that commonly cause this: proxy/nginx or CDN buffering (buffers until a certain size before flushing), gzip/encoding combined with buffering, or the app not flushing after each SSE event. What model and SDK are you using on the backend? Also are you proxying through Cloudflare / ALB / nginx?

ellen: model is gpt-4o-mini (hosted via Redwood), backend is node/express, we route through an internal nginx reverse proxy -> Redwood public endpoint (so we go out to the hosted API).

sam: that makes sense. If nginx or a CDN buffers the response it can hold partial chunks and then forward them when the buffer threshold is hit, which looks like truncated events to a browser EventSource. Two quick checks:
1) run a curl --no-buffer directly from the machine that makes the request to see raw streaming behavior. e.g.:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/…
```
The -N/--no-buffer option disables curl buffering. You should see properly terminated SSE events like `data: {..}\n\n` every time.
2) inspect the proxy: if nginx is in the path, ensure `proxy_buffering off;` or set the header `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on responses. Cloudflare also has options to disable response buffering for streaming routes.

mike: adding to that — also check Transfer-Encoding. The server must flush after each chunk and send the double newline to end an SSE event. Example SSE event the client expects:
```
event: message
data: {\"delta\":\"hello\"}\n\n
```
If you send `data: {\"delta\":\"hello\"}` without the trailing blank line, EventSource won't consider the event complete. Some HTTP stacks auto-buffer until the event delimiter is present.

krish: Also watch for middleware that modifies the body encoding (some gzip middlewares will hold data to compress) — try disabling gzip for the streaming route. For Redwood-hosted endpoints we flush as soon as tokens are generated but if an intermediary re-buffers it will re-chunk.

ellen: infra logs from our side show intermittent upstream aborts around the same times:
```
[2026-04-12T14:03:21Z] nginx: *1021 client 10.1.2.3 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.3, server: poc.example, request: "GET /proxy/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream", host: "poc.example"
```

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-04-12T14:05:00 by @deploy-bot succeeded for poc-backend v0.12.4 (rolled out to 3/3 pods).

sam: OK that upstream message suggests the reverse proxy saw the connection close before the upstream finished sending headers/chunks. Could be a transient network close or a proxy timeout. Check for `proxy_read_timeout` and `send_timeout` too. Also look for intermediate CDNs timing out after X seconds of inactivity (some have default keepalive ~30s).

mike: practical fixes to try quickly:
- On your nginx reverse-proxy add `proxy_buffering off;` for the streaming location.
- Ensure backend includes header `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Cache-Control: no-cache` and sets `X-Accel-Buffering: no`.
- Turn off gzip for the route: `gzip off;`.
- If using Node, call `res.flush()` (or use `compression()` carefully) after writing each SSE event. Example Node snippet:
```
res.write('data: ' + JSON.stringify({delta}) + "\\n\\n");
res.flush();
```

krish: if you can't change the proxy, a workaround is to reduce event sizes or increase heartbeat frequency so the proxy sees regular traffic and won't timeout/buffer; e.g. send a small `:\n` comment line every 10s: `: keepalive\\n\\n`. That keeps connection alive and flushes.

ellen: we'll try the nginx changes and the curl test. Any Redwood-side settings we should check?

sam: on Redwood hosted side we don't have your reverse proxy in the path, so main things are client and your proxy. But if you see `502`/`upstream closed` with a Redwood endpoint, paste the full request id and timestamp and we can look at the logs. If our runtime has to fallback or the model stalls we can dig in.

ellen: after flipping `proxy_buffering off` and adding `X-Accel-Buffering: no` we still had one truncated event but much less frequent. We also disabled gzip for the route — seems promising.

mike: good. If you still see edge-case truncation, send a HAR or raw tcpdump; sometimes a middlebox (corporate firewall) will inject a reset. Also consider switching from EventSource to a websocket or our streaming websocket SDK if you need stronger delivery semantics for POC.

caroline: thanks all — action items: Sam to assist if we provide Redwood request ids, Ellen to run curl --no-buffer + provide HAR if issues persist, Mike/Krish to advise on keepalive and heartbeat pattern. Follow-up sync Thu 10am. :thumbsup:

sam: one more tip for Node devs: `curl --no-buffer` from the same pod as your nginx (not local dev machine) — remote buffering differences matter. Also try `curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" --no-buffer` against the external API to confirm server behavior from your infra plane.

ellen: noted, thanks — will report back after tests. :pray:
